title: One 3D label path, legible: ring numbers, region numbers and part names share one label type, placement and white outlined style; parts coloured by adjacency; RegionLayer.perFrame split into rebuild-on-change and draw
description:
From the user's review of the IMG_4111 naming round (2026-10-24, screenshot of the underside):
1. Dim colours: colour-by-part gives each label the next Palettes.BRIGHT_PATCH entry in label order; the palette has 18 colours and Palette.shadedColor darkens each further round, so with 82 labels most parts are three to five rounds dark. Colour parts by adjacency instead, as regions already are (RegionColouring.colourByNode, Welsh-Powell over the part adjacency graph), so neighbouring parts differ and only bright entries are used. Also the agent's report that region colours go dim after naming until colour-by-part is toggled.
2. Black text: RegionLayer.PART_NAME_COLOUR is Color.BLACK with no outline. glsl/sdf.fs declares borderColor/borderInner/borderOuter but main() never uses them: finish the SDF border so 3D labels draw a white fill with a black border, legible on any background, and use it for part names, ring numbers and TOOL-44's region numbers (named Color constants, no colour arithmetic).
3. Placement: a part name is drawn at its label's stored selection point, offset to the right, so it often sits on a region edge or hangs over the neighbour. Centre each name on its region's visible centre, computed the way TOOL-44 places region numbers (the thickest visible spot), one name per region (a part spanning regions labels each, or its largest).

SCOPE WIDENED (user, 2026-10-24): today three paths draw 3D text (MeshOverlayRuntime.setLabels/drawLabels for ring numbers, a second drawLabels call with RegionLayer's parallel arrays for part names, and RingScene calling font.drawHyperString itself for TOOL-44's region numbers, with different placement, size, colour and depth handling). Make one label type (text plus what it attaches to: a world point, depth-tested, or a region placed at its visible centre), one placement routine (TOOL-44's visible-centre placement moves here out of RegionLayer.perFrame) and one style. Also split RegionLayer.perFrame (~270 lines polling stale flags for about ten jobs) into rebuild-on-change (called by whoever changed the rings, labels, hidden faces or camera) and draw, and move its jobs to their owners: region rebuild, flatness, splits-nothing notes, hidden rings, sliver counts and colouring to RingRegions; label resolution to MeshLabels; one crease lookup shared with RingTool.readyCreases; the explosion's , and . keys become repeating ControlHint rows instead of key polling. RegionLayer keeps deciding what is shown and handing colours and face groups to the runtime.
definition-of-done:
1. With IMG_4111's 82 names, every part is a bright palette colour and no two touching parts share one.
2. Part names, ring numbers and region numbers draw white with a black border.
3. Each name sits inside the region it names, on a visible pixel, centred.
4. Screenshots before/after on the underside and top views; tests for the colouring and placement.
testing-plan:
1. mvn test.
2. Live on tmp/IMG_4111-named.dsl from the craw-77 worktree.
changes-made: One label type, SurfaceLabel (text plus a world point or a face group); HalfEdgeMeshRuntime.placeLabels places both (the visible-centre chamfer moved there from RegionLayer, ties broken to the ridge's middle), MeshOverlayRuntime.drawLabels draws them in one Font.drawHyperStrings pass, white with a black border. RingScene composes ring numbers and RegionLayer.regionLabels (one per region: number and/or part name). Parts coloured by adjacency in MeshLabels.resolve (RegionColouring over part neighbours, Palettes.BRIGHT_PATCH); region rebuild, flatness, notes, slivers, hidden rings and colouring in RingRegions.rebuild/hiddenRingLabels; creases from RingTool.readyCreases; , and . are repeating explode-less/explode-more rows (RegionExplosion.nudge). RegionLayer.perFrame now only shows/drops, rebuilds on ring revision (keeping craw-79's no-mask-change rule) and steps the explosion. Regions, fingerprints and saved .dsl unchanged on fertility_rings and IMG_4111; mvn test 674/0.

Rework after review: SurfaceLabel removed. 3D text is HyperString: an anchor plus anchorCamera (a Camera3D projects the world point and hides the string through Camera3D.pointVisibility, which HalfEdgeMeshRuntime implements as visiblePixel, a projection and depth test with anchorDepthLift) and a shown flag. Region labels are 2D-anchored HyperStrings whose anchor RegionLayer sets from HalfEdgeMeshRuntime.faceGroupCentre (the chamfer search) when the camera, regions or hidden faces change. render.model holds and draws no labels. HyperWord carries its style (borderColor, borderPixels); Font.drawAnchoredStrings lays out and draws the shown strings in one pass and SDFTexture.setWordBorder sets the border uniforms per word; the stamping and the border overload are gone. sdf.fs draws the band from borderInner to borderOuter screen pixels on the true-distance channel, off while borderColor is transparent (the dead logo border arguments were removed). Atlas regenerated with msdf-atlas-gen 1.4.0 (MIT, github.com/Chlumsky/msdf-atlas-gen): msdf-atlas-gen -font ixdar-app/src/main/resources/res/OpenSans_Condensed-SemiBold.ttf -chars '[32, 126]' -type mtsdf -size 128 -pxrange 48 -yorigin bottom -dimensions 2048 2048 -format png -imageout opensans.png -json opensans.json, JSON re-indented; em 128 with range 48 reaches about 3.5 screen px past a glyph at the 26 px label row, and the plane bounds carry that padding. Font keeps blank glyphs (space) that the new atlas lists without atlas bounds. Synced onto master after craw-79 (its no-mask-change rule kept in RegionLayer.rebuild). mvn test 679/0.

Ring numbers no longer show through the mesh: RingTool.placeRingNumbers (run in RingScene's 2D pass, only when the camera view, framebuffer or rings changed) anchors each number on a point of its own loop, the one nearest the ring's on-screen centroid whose two faces both face the camera and which Camera3D.pointVisibility finds unhidden (at most 8 depth reads per ring), with a 3-pixel depth tie instead of the ring's outer radius as lift; a ring seen only from behind or from inside the body gets no number. Test RegionControlAutomationTest.aRingNumberSitsOnTheLoopFacingTheCameraAndHidesFromInsideAndBehind. Live on IMG_4111: from the tail side numbers sit on their visible loops; from inside the tail 0 numbers at one spot and 1 at another (ring 61 on a fold whose own faces turn toward the eye).

Orbit lag with numbers on fixed. Profile (numbers on, drag on IMG_4111): HalfEdgeMeshRuntime.visiblePixel's one glReadPixels per point was 16% of samples, mostly from placeRingNumbers; the region face-id grid and chamfer cost almost nothing. Now (1) GL.readDepth became readDepths(rect) and visiblePixel reads the whole depth buffer once per drawn frame (reset in render) and looks points up; (2) region labels no longer use a screen-space visible centre: each is a 3D-anchored HyperString on RingRegions.regionLabelPoint, the centroid of the region's face most face steps from its rings, taken from the ring-step flood measureFlatness already runs and carried for regions an update leaves alone; faceGroupCentre, setCentreGroups, faceIndexGrid and the chamfer constants are gone; (3) ring numbers keep their loop point while the camera moves (RingScene.cameraStill) and are re-chosen once it holds still; (4) visiblePixel inverts depth through the surface pass's planes and also refuses a point the pixel shows past (background or another sheet beyond a silhouette), so a label on a back-facing deepest face is hidden, not floated off the edge. Drag of 60 frames, numbers, region numbers and part names on: 5401/5753/6264 ms before, 3230-3626 ms after; labels off 2672 ms. Named labels pick their own region and part: underside 17/17, tail side 9/9 (fewer named labels show than with screen-space placement, since a region whose deepest face is turned away is not labelled, per ruling).
review-summary:
Ring numbers, part names and region numbers are now HyperStrings anchored in 3D or on a region's visible centre, drawn white with a shader border from a regenerated wide-range atlas; parts are coloured by adjacency and RegionLayer rebuilds on change.
Labels were dim, black and on region edges.
